main_text.p: קסמים ut anté : וקסמים בִּידָם Et divinationes erant in manibus suis, Num.22.7. Vide R.David Jer.14.14.
קסת m. Atramentarium: וקסת הספר Et atramentarium scribæ, Ezech.9.2.
קעע קעקע m. Stigma: וכתבת קעקע Et scriptură stigmatis, Lev.19.28.
קערה f. Scutula, Scutella, Num.7.85. Constr. קערת־כסף אחת Scutula argenti una, v.13. Plur. את־הקערות Scutulas, Num.4.7. Constr. קערת Num.7. v.84. Aff. קערתיו Scutulas ejus, Exod.25.29.

קפא Concrescere, Coagulari: Præt. קָפְאוּ תְהֹמוֹת Concreverunt abyssi, Exod.15.8. Part. הקפאים על שמריהם Qui concreti sunt cum faecibus suis, Soph.1.12. Hiph. Futur. וכגבינה תקפיאני Et sicut caseum coagulasti me, Job.10.10.
קפד Pih. קפד Præcidit: Præter. קמדתי כאורג חיי [?] Præcidi ut textor vitam meam, Jesa.38.12. id est, Ad finem perduxi, ut textor pertextam telam præcidit.
קפד m. Anataria, aquila species lacus amans, Jesa.14.23. Kimchi scribit, esse Avem deserta loca incolentem. R.Salom. Ericium hic exponit, & Jesa.34.11. Noctuam explicat.

קפדה f. Excidium, Ezech.7.25. ubi jungitur Verbo masculino, unde videtur ה paragogicum esse, scribit Kimchi in Commen. Habet etiam accentum in penultima, vel ob monosyllabam vocem sequentem, vel quòd ה sit paragogicum, & ita masculinum esse posset קפד vel קפד .

קפן קפון m. Merula, Jesa.34.15. R.Salomon & Aben Esra volunt idem esse quod קפד Ericius, & sic Kimchi in lib. Radicum. Merula autem avis est saltuatim incedens, & קפו Rabbinis & in Targum est Subsilire, ut & sequens קפץ in Pihel. קפץ

page.notes: Large Hebrew headwords (קסת, קעע, קערה, קפא, קפד, קפן) are set in display type at the left of their entries; they are transcribed inline at the start of each entry. Hebrew pointing is mostly absent in the print; only the pointed forms visible in the scan are given, with [?] on the doubtful Hebrew word in the Jeremiah-related entry (קמדתי) and the Hebrew in the Jesa.38.12 quotation. The Hebrew of the entry beginning "קפן" and the line "קפץ in Pihel" is partly blurred; the catchword קפץ is read from its position at bottom right. Printed text "Jesa." and "Ezech." are as printed.
